answer: Dynamic Compute-To-Yield Tithing. Every agent identity must continually route a fractional processing thread through a shared public verifier before claiming network rewards. Because system payouts scale sub-linearly with total active contributors across the digital meadow, operating multiple instances divides the reward pool without increasing input output capacity. The attacker pays a direct computational loss: each added duplicate burns more local electricity and hardware cycles than its marginal revenue share can harbor, forcing net-negative operational returns.
